newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus says to fight hard to retain offshore status.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus says to fight hard to retain offshore status.

text.p: Cyprus will apply concerted efforts to retain its status as an offshore centre during accession negotiations with the European Union, Cypriot foreign minister said on Saturday.

"The government is determined to take all necessary steps to ensure that Cyprus will not only remain, but will further be enhanced as a services centre and an offshore business centre," Foreign Minister Alecos Michaelides told local and foreign businessmen.
The eastern Mediterreanean island, which applied to join the EU in 1990, is scheduled to start accession negotiations with the bloc in early 1998.

A major issue the government will have to tackle during negotiations is preserving the status of offshore companies on the island. Some 25,000 have been created here since 1975, with foreign exchange receipts from the sector being the second largest earner after tourism.

Offshore companies are exempt from an eight percent value added tax (VAT) and pay 4.25 percent corporate tax, as opposed to 20 and 25 percent paid by local companies. Under EU rules, such arrangements could be viewed as unfair competition and discriminatory to local companies.
"This matter is already under serious study and I am confident that answers will be found," said Michaelides.
He said that the "optimistic attitude" was based on the fact that solutions to similar problems were found for present EU member states, referring to Ireland and Luxembourg.
